component: packages/contracts (date validation across rfq, rental, project, maintenance, billing, quotation, transport)
previous_assumption: assumed date fields (requestedStartDate/validityDate, startDate/endDate, billingPeriodStart/End, etc.) needed no special validation since they were simple calendar dates
correction: Every z.string().date() field in the app had zero validation, front or back -- no min on any date input, no cross-field ordering check anywhere except Auction's endsAt greater than startsAt refine. Fixed per-entity, not uniformly: Requirement/Rental/Quotation get a not-in-the-past check plus ordering (validityDate less-or-equal startDate, endDate greater-or-equal startDate); Project/Maintenance get ordering only, no not-in-the-past rule, since backfilling an already-underway project or logging past maintenance is normal (confirmed by seed-demo-data.ts itself); Billing gets ordering only (billingPeriodEnd/dueDate), no past/future rule, since backdating an invoice period is normal and seed-demo-data.ts deliberately paidDates into the future; Transport gets only actualDate-not-in-future, no ordering against plannedDate (dispatch can legitimately happen earlier or later than planned); Auction was deliberately left alone beyond its existing refine, since both seed-demo-data.ts and acceptance-flows.test.ts deliberately create an auction that already started (immediate-bidding demo), so startsAt-not-in-the-past would have broken a real, intentional capability. Also: cross-field ordering cannot be a Zod refine on a partial UPDATE schema since either date may be absent from the payload -- RequirementService.updateRequirement and ProjectService.updateProject check the merged final values (update.field-or-existing.field) instead. And: seed-demo-data.ts and acceptance-flows.test.ts both call application services directly in-process, bypassing Zod validation entirely (only apps/api presentation/routes.ts calls parseWithSchema) -- so neither the seed script nor any existing unit test could ever be broken by adding a schema-level refine; only real HTTP callers (the frontend, or a direct API call) are affected.
